rendered:
Under the US Advanced Battery Consortium standards, an EV battery reaches the end of its usable life when its current cell capacity is less than[1] 80%[2] of the rated capacity.[3]
Such end-of-life EV batteries can be reused or repurposed, recycled, or disposed of in landfills, though landfill disposal would cause serious environmental issues.[4]
Repurposing gives the batteries a second life, reconfiguring them for applications such as grid energy storage and behind-the-meter energy storage.[5]
The review says that all of these batteries, whether or not they are reused first, eventually need to be recycled.[6]
